question: Which of these common items spoils easily if left outside the fridge in warm weather?

options.A: Dry white rice
options.B: Canned tomato paste
options.C: Granulated sugar
options.D: Fresh milk

question: What are the three classic steps in Kurt Lewin's model of change?

options.A: Unfreezing, moving, and refreezing
options.B: Denial, anger, and acceptance
options.C: Planning, executing, and evaluating
options.D: Assessing, diagnosing, and treating

explanation: Classic nursing management! Think of it like melting an ice block, shaping it into something new, and freezing it solid again. [learn more](GST319_U2_T5#GST319_U2_T5_h3)

question: What exactly is an element of cost in healthcare finance?

options.A: The price charged to a patient for bed space

options.C: The total profit made by a hospital ward
options.D: A way to categorize and break down expenses

explanation: Think of cost elements as simple buckets or categories we use to group and track money spent on things like staff salaries and ward materials. You've got this! [learn more](GST322_U2_T2#GST322_U2_T2_h1)

question: Why is it important to quickly report and investigate serious adverse events following immunization (AEFIs)?

options.A: To increase the total number of children attending clinic
options.B: To protect public confidence and maintain safety standards
options.C: To eliminate the need for cold chain temperature logs
options.D: To ensure that nurses receive financial compensation

explanation: Acting fast and being transparent stops panic, squashes false rumors, and keeps trust high in our healthcare services. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T75#GNS214_U1_T75_h6)

question: A nurse puts on gloves before emptying a patient's urine bag. Which part of the chain of infection is the nurse blocking?

options.A: Reservoir
options.B: Mode of transmission
options.C: Infectious agent
options.D: Susceptible host

explanation: You got it! Gloves act as a physical barrier, stopping the germs from hitching a ride onto the nurse's hands. [learn more](GST114_U2_T5#GST114_U2_T5_h2)

question: How does unit dispensing improve financial transparency for patients?

options.A: Medication prices are standardized across all states
options.B: Hospital care becomes completely free of charge
options.C: Invoices are calculated based on hospital stay duration
options.D: Patients pay only for the exact doses administered

explanation: Instead of buying an entire pack of fifty tablets when only five are needed, the patient only pays for those five doses. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T4#GNS215_U1_T4_h2)

question: What is an early or forced marriage?

options.A: Any wedding that takes place without religious approval
options.B: A marital arrangement organized strictly by government officials
options.C: A union where one or both parties are under 18 without full consent
options.D: Any marriage occurring between individuals from different tribes

explanation: Spot on! Early and forced marriage means minors are pushed into a union without giving free and wise personal consent. As nurses, protecting the young is key! [learn more](GNS312_U1_T13#GNS312_U1_T13_h1)

question: Where do you aim when giving a subcutaneous injection?

options.A: Deep inside the main skeletal muscle tissue
options.B: Directly into the circulating bloodstream
options.C: Into the layer of fat beneath the skin
options.D: Between the outer epidermis and the dermis

explanation: You've got this! Subcutaneous simply means 'under the skin,' targeting the fatty layer right beneath the dermis. Great job remembering your tissue layers! [learn more](GNS125_U3_T7#GNS125_U3_T7_h1)

question: Why must nurses tailor assessment tools to fit a degenerative patient's physical limits?

options.A: To make the test results legally binding in a court of law
options.B: To eliminate the need for family members to be present
options.C: To ensure the patient does not get tired or frustrated during testing
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing paper questionnaires

explanation: If a patient is exhausted, test scores won't show their true ability. Matching their energy levels keeps the assessment accurate and stress-free. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T18#GNS222_U4_T18_h3)

question: Why do doctors generally avoid estrogen-containing contraceptives for women with sickle cell disease after childbirth?

options.A: They immediately stop all breast milk production
options.B: They cause permanent changes in maternal voice pitch
options.C: They increase the risk of dangerous blood clots
options.D: They destroy the effectiveness of folic acid supplements

explanation: Correct! Estrogen raises clot risks, and since postpartum mums with sickle cell are already prone to clots, it's best to steer clear. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T005#GNS226_U4_T005_h6)

question: What actually happens in the brain during a seizure?

options.A: A sudden, uncontrolled burst of electrical activity in the brain
options.B: A permanent loss of brain tissue caused by low oxygen
options.C: A complete cessation of all brainwave activity
options.D: A localized infection of the outer meninges

explanation: Think of a seizure like an electrical power surge in the brain. Brain cells suddenly fire signals all at once, which temporarily overloads the system and affects how a person moves, feels, or acts. You've got this! [learn more](GNS223_U6_T3#GNS223_U6_T3_h1)

question: When should you wear medical gloves while caring for a patient?

options.A: Only when performing surgical procedures
options.B: Whenever entering any patient room
options.C: During all routine vital sign measurements
options.D: When anticipating contact with blood or body fluids

explanation: Spot on! Wear gloves whenever there is a chance your hands might touch blood, body fluids, mucous membranes, or broken skin. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h3)

question: Which clinical sign is most characteristic of kwashiorkor?

options.A: Severe muscle wasting with no body fat at all
options.B: Rapid overgrowth of the long bones
options.C: Generalized pitting edema and skin changes
options.D: An extremely high fever with sudden seizures

explanation: Kwashiorkor happens when a child lacks enough protein. A classic giveaway is swelling (edema) in the body and noticeable skin changes. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T012#GNS227_U7_T012_h7)

question: Why do we actually study nursing theories in school? What is their main job?

options.A: To dictate how much medication a patient should receive
options.B: To eliminate the need for doctor and nurse collaboration
options.C: To guide clinical practice and provide a scientific base
options.D: To replace hospital policies and procedure manuals

explanation: Think of nursing theories as the bedrock of our profession! They give us a clear, scientific reason for the way we care for patients every single day. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T6#GNS112_U3_T6_h1)

question: What does a cardiotocograph (CTG) machine monitor continuously during labour?

options.A: Maternal core temperature and blood sugar
options.B: Amount of amniotic fluid and bladder volume
options.C: Cervical dilation and pelvic bone width
options.D: Foetal heart rate and uterine contractions

explanation: A CTG machine tracks the baby's heartbeat on one channel and the mother's labour contractions on the other channel simultaneously. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T003#GNS226_U4_T003_h4)

question: According to standard infection control rules, how often should primary IV tubing be changed?

options.A: 24 to 36 hours
options.B: Only until the bag empties
options.C: 72 to 96 hours
options.D: Every 7 days exactly

explanation: Spot on! Standard primary lines are generally swapped out every 3 to 4 days (72 to 96 hours) to keep bacteria from building up. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T3#GNS212_U4_T3_h7)

question: What tool can nurses use to help patients estimate portion sizes more accurately?

options.A: A standard household measuring cup for liquid medications only
options.B: A complex laboratory blood test for vitamin levels
options.C: Visual aids like food models or picture charts
options.D: Strict financial receipts from local grocery stores

explanation: Patients often struggle to describe portion sizes in grams or cups, so visual aids make it easier for them to show how much they ate. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T002#GNS227_U5_T002_h8)

question: Which emergency during the third stage of labor requires an immediate hospital transfer?

options.A: Mild postpartum fatigue
options.B: Normal placental separation
options.C: Transient shivering after birth
options.D: Severe postpartum hemorrhage

explanation: Heavy bleeding after delivery can quickly become life-threatening. Stop the bleeding and get the mother to the hospital fast! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T3#GNS225_U3_T3_h6)

question: What is a major hazard of using physical restraints on an older adult?

options.A: Immediate strengthening of lower limb bone density and balance
options.B: Increased risk of muscle weakness, agitation, and severe injury
options.C: Complete prevention of accidental falls in all clinical settings
options.D: Permanent restoration of full cognitive function and memory

explanation: Restraints do not prevent falls safely; instead, they lead to rapid muscle wasting, emotional distress, and worse injuries when patients try to get free. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T8#GNS225_U5_T8_h5)

question: What is one of the biggest roadblocks stopping teenagers from seeking reproductive health care at clinics?

options.A: Judgmental healthcare attitudes and cultural taboos
options.B: A complete lack of biological changes during puberty
options.C: Immunity to all forms of sexually transmitted infections
options.D: Strict laws requiring parental consent for all general check-ups

explanation: Too often, young people stay away from clinics because they are scared health workers will scold, judge, or gossip about them. As nurses, we must be welcoming! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T3#GNS216_U1_T3_h5)

question: Which of these grains is naturally safe to eat on a gluten-free diet?

options.A: Spelt
options.B: Barley
options.C: Rye
options.D: Quinoa

explanation: Quinoa is a fantastic pseudocereal that is naturally free of gluten. Perfect for safe and healthy meal planning! [learn more](GNS227_U6_T011#GNS227_U6_T011_h3)

question: What kind of conflict happens entirely inside your own head?

options.A: Intrapersonal conflict
options.B: Intragroup conflict
options.C: Intergroup conflict
options.D: Interpersonal conflict

explanation: Intrapersonal conflict is that inner battle we all face—like when you're trying to make a tough personal choice or dealing with stress all by yourself. [learn more](GST321_U5_T1#GST321_U5_T1_h2)

question: How should you position your patient's head during an eye wash?

options.A: Tilted slightly toward the affected side
options.B: Tilted firmly toward the unaffected side
options.C: Positioned flat and facing straight up
options.D: Tilted backward as far as the neck allows

explanation: Tilting toward the bad side ensures the dirty runoff flows away off the face instead of spilling into the healthy eye. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T12#GNS122_U1_T12_h4)

question: What is a major benefit of using indirect learning experiences (like simulations) in nursing school?

options.A: They are always more expensive to run than actual bedside teaching
options.B: They completely replace the need for any clinical hospital rotations
options.C: They provide safe environments to explore complex scenarios without harming patients
options.D: They eliminate all forms of student evaluation and grading stress

explanation: Indirect experiences let you practice tricky situations safely so you feel ready when you step onto the real ward. [learn more](GST321_U8_T5#GST321_U8_T5_h3)

question: Which service is a primary responsibility within school health services?

options.A: Manufacturing pharmaceutical drugs
options.B: Routine health screenings and first aid
options.C: Issuing national identity cards
options.D: Performing major surgical operations

explanation: School nurses focus on preventive checks, early detection, and managing minor injuries or emergencies on site. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h2)

question: What is the difference between abdominal bloating and abdominal distension?

options.A: Bloating is a feeling of fullness, while distension is visible swelling of the abdomen.
options.B: Bloating only occurs in the stomach, while distension only occurs in the rectum.
options.C: Distension is caused by swallowed air, whereas bloating is caused by poor hygiene.
options.D: Bloating causes sharp pain, while distension is completely painless.

explanation: Bloating is how the patient *feels* (internal pressure), while distension is what you can actually *see* (a swollen tummy). Easy distinction! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T10#GNS212_U1_T10_h4)

question: Why is regular follow-up care essential for a patient recovering from hyperemesis gravidarum?

options.A: To monitor her weight, hydration, and lab values for stability
options.B: To measure the exact length of the baby using a tape measure
options.C: To make sure she is exercising at the gym twice a week
options.D: To change her prescribed prenatal vitamins every single week

explanation: Frequent checks allow healthcare providers to catch returning dehydration or weight loss early before hospitalization becomes necessary. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T012#GNS226_U2_T012_h7)

question: Which exercise choice is safest and best for a client with an inflammatory joint disease?

options.A: Low-impact aerobic exercise like swimming
options.B: High-impact running on hard asphalt surfaces
options.C: Competitive contact sports and wrestling
options.D: Heavy weightlifting with maximal resistance

explanation: Low-impact activities like swimming let clients stay active and keep their joints flexible without pounding them with heavy mechanical stress. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T11#GNS222_U1_T11_h7)

question: What is the very first step in a standard progressive discipline process?

options.A: Informal verbal warning
options.B: Immediate termination
options.C: Formal written warning
options.D: Temporary suspension

explanation: Progressive discipline starts gently with a private, verbal conversation to address minor issues early. [learn more](GST321_U1_T22#GST321_U1_T22_h5)

question: In the famous 'CAUTION' warning signs of cancer, what does the letter 'U' stand for?

options.A: Unexplained weight gain
options.B: Urinary tract infection
options.C: Unusual bleeding or discharge
options.D: Ulceration of the skin

explanation: Remember CAUTION! The 'U' reminds us to never ignore unexplained bleeding or discharge from any part of the body. Keep that in your nursing toolkit! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T15#GNS214_U1_T15_h6)

question: Why does showing great clinical skills make someone a better leader?

options.A: It allows them to work completely independently of doctors.
options.B: It prevents patients from ever filing formal complaints.
options.C: It exempts them from doing any paperwork during their shifts.
options.D: It sets a benchmark that encourages staff to strive for excellence.

explanation: Actions speak louder than words! When your team sees you performing nursing procedures with skill and care, they feel inspired to bring their A-game too. [learn more](GST321_U3_T4#GST321_U3_T4_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a recommended strategy for improving PTA effectiveness in school health? (Look for the exception)

options.A: Ensuring transparent accounting of all funds raised for projects
options.B: Focusing meetings solely on demanding financial levies without explanations
options.C: Inviting community health nurses to give health talks during meetings
options.D: Partnering with local health centers for regular student screenings

explanation: Focusing only on money without engaging parents in health education or being transparent causes apathy and drives parents away. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T5#GNS225_U4_T5_h7)

question: Why do some sleeping pills sometimes fail to give patients truly refreshing rest?

options.A: They permanently damage the brainstem respiratory control centers
options.B: They cause severe dehydration and electrolyte imbalance during sleep
options.C: They distort normal sleep stages by suppressing deep and rapid eye movement sleep
options.D: They cause the patient to sleep for less than two hours per night

explanation: Certain sleeping pills mess with your natural sleep cycle, blocking you from getting enough of that crucial deep sleep and REM rest. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T1#GNS223_U6_T1_h2)

question: Which agency coordinates national disaster management in Nigeria?

options.A: Nigerian Union_of Journalists
options.B: Federal Road Safety Corps exclusively

question: Why does batch cooking help save money?

options.A: It guarantees that food will never spoil under any condition
options.B: It requires buying expensive kitchen appliances upfront
options.C: It forces family members to eat less food overall
options.D: It reduces energy consumption and limits ingredient waste

explanation: Spot on! Cooking larger pots at once uses less cooking gas or kerosene and ensures ingredients get used up before going bad. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T004#GNS227_U3_T004_h3)

question: An environmental health officer is checking a suspected food poisoning outbreak at a local canteen. What is the very first step before any lab testing can start?

options.A: Collecting a representative sample using sterile equipment and proper cold storage
options.B: Immediately closing down all food businesses operating in that neighborhood
options.C: Administering intravenous antibiotics to all customers who ate at the canteen
options.D: Spraying chemical disinfectants across the entire kitchen and dining area

explanation: Brilliant! Lab tests are only as good as the sample you send them. Proper sterile collection and keeping it cold are always step one. [learn more](GST114_U5_T5#GST114_U5_T5_h5)

question: Why do we use a clean razor blade from a birth kit to cut the baby's cord?

options.A: To speed up the drying of the remaining cord stump
options.B: To make the procedure painless for the newborn baby
options.C: To prevent tetanus and other bacterial infections
options.D: To ensure the cord detaches within the first 24 hours

explanation: Using a clean, sterile blade stops nasty germs from getting into the fresh cord vessels. That's our main defense against neonatal tetanus! You've got this. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T008#GNS226_U3_T008_h1)

question: As a nurse, what is an essential step when assessing a patient who might have a contagious infection?

options.A: Taking a detailed history of recent travel, occupation, and contacts
options.B: Isolating the patient in a surgical suite immediately
options.C: Measuring the patient's blood pressure every fifteen minutes
options.D: Administering broad-spectrum antibiotics before checking lab results

explanation: You're building great clinical detective skills! Asking about travel, work, and who they've been around helps track down where the bug came from. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T3#GNS313_U1_T3_h5)

question: What is the primary focus of palliative care for older adults with advanced illnesses?

options.A: Quickly discharging the patient from home care
options.B: Maximizing comfort and quality of life
options.C: Stopping all forms of nursing communication
options.D: Finding a complete cure for every diagnosis

explanation: Palliative care isn't about curing; it's all about easing pain and distressing symptoms so the patient can live their remaining days with dignity and comfort. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T3#GNS324_U3_T3_h8)

question: What is the biggest risk if a child receives the wrong, uncalculated dose of an antiparasitic drug?

options.A: Under-dosing can cause treatment failure and drug resistance
options.B: Incorrect doses prevent topical creams from working
options.C: Weight-based dosing only matters for intravenous antibiotics
options.D: Over-dosing always leads to permanent blindness

explanation: Always double-check those pediatric weights! Giving too little medication might leave some hardy parasites alive, helping them bounce back stronger and drug-resistant. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T1#GNS215_U6_T1_h7)

question: Which sign is a classic giveaway of an opioid overdose?

options.A: Pinpoint pupils
options.B: Extreme pupil dilation
options.C: Uncontrollable muscle tremors
options.D: Severe skin redness and sweating

explanation: Spot on! Tiny, pinpoint pupils combined with slow breathing are classic red flags for opioid overdose. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T13#GNS313_U3_T13_h4)

question: What is a major effect of severe heatstroke on the body's cells?

options.A: Disruption of vital enzymatic reactions and cellular function
options.B: Complete cessation of electrical activity in the skeletal muscles
options.C: Rapid production of large quantities of protective body fat
options.D: Permanent freezing of blood vessels in the upper extremities

explanation: Extreme heat scrambles the delicate proteins and enzymes our cells need to work. Cooling the patient down quickly is a true medical emergency priority! [learn more](GNS315_U2_T4#GNS315_U2_T4_h5)

question: Why is immunization considered a fundamental component of Primary Health Care?

options.A: It is delivered exclusively inside major tertiary teaching hospitals
options.B: It replaces the need for proper sanitation and clean drinking water
options.C: It provides affordable, community-based disease prevention for all
options.D: It focuses on treating advanced stages of communicable diseases

explanation: Primary Health Care aims to bring essential health services as close as possible to where people live, making preventive measures like vaccines easily accessible. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h1)

question: Which test is usually ordered first to look for ovarian cysts or fibroids in the womb?

options.A: Abdominal X-ray
options.B: Magnetic resonance angiography
options.C: CT scan
options.D: Pelvic ultrasound

explanation: Well done! Pelvic ultrasound uses safe sound waves to give a clear picture of internal reproductive organs without using radiation. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T7#GNS311_U1_T7_h4)

question: What is your very first nursing action if you suspect a transfusion reaction?

options.A: Increase the intravenous fluid flow rate
options.B: Collect a fresh blood sample for typing
options.C: Administer a dose of prescribed antihistamines
options.D: Stop the blood transfusion immediately

explanation: Patient safety first! Stopping the infusion right away prevents any more incompatible red blood cells from flowing into the patient. You'll master this clinical skill in no time! [learn more](GNS111_U2_T2#GNS111_U2_T2_h6)

question: What does a mixed methods research study combine?

options.A: Hospital budgets and staffing rosters
options.B: Traditional habits and modern myths
options.C: Physician opinions and nursing guesses
options.D: Quantitative and qualitative approaches

explanation: You guessed it—mixed methods brings together both numerical data and narrative stories into one study! [learn more](GNS217_U1_T2#GNS217_U1_T2_h7)

question: In a standard three-chamber chest tube setup, what is the job of the very first chamber?

options.A: To filter out all bacteria entering from the room air
options.B: To add sterile water directly into the patient's lung tissue
options.C: To control the exact wall suction pressure applied to the unit
options.D: To collect and measure fluid draining from the patient

explanation: Chamber one is simply the catch basin. It safely collects whatever fluid, blood, or pus drains out so you can measure it easily. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T15#GNS213_U2_T15_h3)

question: What do we call any sexual act forced upon someone against their will?

options.A: Psychological neglect
options.B: Sexual violence
options.C: Socio-cultural isolation
options.D: Domestic auditing

explanation: That's correct! Any non-consensual sexual contact or coercion is classified as sexual violence. Knowing these terms helps you advocate better for your patients. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T10#GNS312_U4_T10_h4)

question: What is the main difference between protozoa and helminths?

options.A: Protozoa are always visible to the naked eye unlike helminths
options.B: Protozoa are single-celled organisms while helminths are parasitic worms
options.C: Protozoa only infect animals while helminths infect humans
options.D: Protozoa only live in soil while helminths only live in water

explanation: Easy rule to remember: protozoa are tiny, single-celled microbes, while helminths are actual parasitic worms. You're doing great! [learn more](GST114_U6_T3#GST114_U6_T3_h2)

question: Why are standards essential for a nurse manager within the control process?

options.A: They provide a baseline measurement to evaluate actual nursing practice
options.B: They completely eliminate the need for shift handovers
options.C: They prevent patients from ever complaining about care
options.D: They dictate the exact salary scale for each department

explanation: A standard gives managers a clear, agreed-upon target to check if the care being delivered matches what is expected. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h1)

question: What is a major *indirect* cost associated with a physical disability?

options.A: The retail price of a custom wheelchair
options.B: Lost income due to unemployment and workplace barriers
options.C: Direct consultation fees at the clinic
options.D: Buying prescription anti-inflammatory drugs

explanation: Indirect costs are about what you *fail to earn* because of missed work, job loss, or barriers to employment—not direct store purchases. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T12#GNS225_U5_T12_h4)

question: Which dimension of quality care ensures that clinical treatments are based on proven scientific guidelines?

options.A: Safety
options.B: Accessibility
options.C: Acceptability
options.D: Effectiveness

explanation: Brilliant! Effectiveness focuses on using evidence-based practices so that our nursing interventions actually achieve the best health outcomes for the patient. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T4#GNS312_U5_T4_h2)

question: What usually happens to public health funding when the national economy goes through a tough patch?

options.A: Private clinics take over all public patients
options.B: Hospitals receive a sudden surge of extra grants
options.C: The cost of medical care drops to zero everywhere
options.D: Government health budgets are often reduced

explanation: Spot on. When money is tight nationally, governments collect less revenue and unfortunately tend to slash public sector budgets, including healthcare. [learn more](GST322_U5_T1#GST322_U5_T1_h2)

question: When giving ear drops to an adult patient, how should you pull the outer ear (pinna)?

options.A: Forward and down
options.B: Down and back
options.C: Straight outward
options.D: Up and back

explanation: A classic clinical tip! For adults, pulling the pinna up and back straightens out the wiggly ear canal so the drops flow smoothly all the way down. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h7)

question: What is a major practical challenge to good clinical supervision in busy Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: An excess of well-trained administrative supervisors
options.B: Complete absence of any clinical policies or guidelines
options.C: Heavy staff workloads and severe staff shortages
options.D: Too much free time available during morning shifts

explanation: We all know how packed the wards can get! High patient numbers and few staff members make it tough to find time for mentoring. [learn more](GST321_U1_T17#GST321_U1_T17_h6)

question: A nursing mum in the clinic needs affordable protein options available in local Nigerian markets. What should you suggest?

options.A: Processed canned biscuits
options.B: Imported energy drink powders
options.C: Packaged artificial sweeteners
options.D: Beans, crayfish, and lean fish

explanation: Local proteins like beans, crayfish, and fish are budget-friendly, easily accessible, and provide wonderful amino acids for lactation. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T013#GNS227_U2_T013_h7)

question: What acid-base imbalance can develop from continuous stomach suctioning?

options.A: Metabolic acidosis
options.B: Respiratory acidosis
options.C: Metabolic alkalosis
options.D: Respiratory alkalosis

explanation: Sucking out large amounts of acidic stomach fluid leaves the body with excess base, leading to metabolic alkalosis. You're mastering body chemistry! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T3#GNS213_U3_T3_h8)

question: Why must patients constantly rotate their injection sites?

options.A: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing new syringes
options.B: To prevent localized skin hardening and altered drug absorption
options.C: To stop the needle from becoming dull during repeated use
options.D: To ensure the medication reaches the bloodstream much faster

explanation: Using the exact same spot over and over can cause fatty lumps (lipohypertrophy) and mess up how the drug is absorbed. Moving around keeps the skin healthy! [learn more](GNS125_U3_T7#GNS125_U3_T7_h4)

question: Why should a nurse in a public hospital care about civil service regulations?

options.A: It exempts the nurse from complying with the nursing and midwifery council acts
options.B: It allows the nurse to bypass hospital management during emergency procedures
options.C: It grants the nurse the authority to promote other junior staff members
options.D: It helps align clinical practice with administrative compliance and protects professional rights

explanation: Knowing your workplace rules helps you stay on the right side of management while protecting your rights on the job. You've got this! [learn more](GST321_U10_T1#GST321_U10_T1_h1)

question: Why must patient assessment in palliative care be an ongoing, continuous process?

options.A: Because terminal illnesses and symptom experiences change rapidly over time
options.B: Because laboratory values fluctuate constantly during end-of-life care
options.C: Because hospital regulations require daily documentation updates
options.D: Because family members frequently change their minds about treatment

explanation: As serious illnesses progress, new symptoms pop up and emotional states shift. Constant checking and reassessing help us adjust care to keep the patient as comfortable as possible. Keep shining! [learn more](GNS321_U4_T11#GNS321_U4_T11_h2)

question: What is the main idea behind social learning theory?

options.A: Building personal mental maps of human anatomy
options.B: Observing and imitating the actions of role models
options.C: Taking computer-based exams to test long-term memory
options.D: Receiving direct financial rewards for good test scores

explanation: We learn so much just by watching the people around us! Social learning proves we pick up habits by observing mentors and seeing what works for them. [learn more](GST321_U8_T1#GST321_U8_T1_h7)

question: Why is it so important for you as a nurse to understand how a community functions?

options.A: To prescribe medications without needing a doctor
options.B: To manage hospital financial budgets and staff salaries
options.C: To understand how daily living conditions affect people's health
options.D: To diagnose rare genetic diseases in hospital laboratories

explanation: Spot on! The environment and everyday resources around your patients shape their health just as much as any medicine you give them. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T4#GNS225_U1_T4_h1)

question: A ward records 50 patients with hypertension out of 200 patients screened. What percentage is that?

options.A: 20 percent
options.B: 10 percent
options.C: 25 percent
options.D: 50 percent

explanation: Brilliant! 50 divided by 200 gives you 0.25, which translates nicely to 25 percent. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T8#GNS217_U4_T8_h2)

question: Why is building a warm, trusting relationship so important during a health history chat?

options.A: It speeds up the hospital discharge process significantly
options.B: It eliminates the need for a physical examination entirely
options.C: It guarantees the patient will take all prescribed medications
options.D: It encourages the patient to share sensitive details honestly

explanation: You got it! When patients trust you and feel safe, they'll open up about the things that really matter for their care. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T3#GNS222_U3_T3_h1)

question: You walk into a stuffy ward, fling the windows open to let in fresh air, and tidy up a messy bedside. Whose classic nursing theory are you putting into action?

options.A: Hildegard Peplau
options.B: Florence Nightingale
options.C: Dorothea Orem
options.D: Virginia Henderson

explanation: Brilliant! Opening windows and clearing away dirt are the ultimate trademark moves of Nightingale's Environmental Theory. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T6#GNS112_U3_T6_h2)

question: What is a simple, practical habit to ensure a patient gets a wide variety of helpful antioxidants and plant nutrients?

options.A: Eating a colorful variety of different fruits and vegetables every day
options.B: Eating the exact same single vegetable for every meal to track intake
options.C: Choosing only white and beige foods because they digest more easily
options.D: Relying entirely on multi-vitamin pills while avoiding fresh produce

explanation: Spot on! Different plant colors mean different health-boosting compounds, so eating a rainbow is always the best prescription. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T004#GNS227_U4_T004_h6)

question: A patient with an undiagnosed chronic cough is admitted to your ward. What precautions should you use first?

options.A: Standard Precautions
options.B: Strict reverse isolation
options.C: Contact Precautions only
options.D: No precautions until lab results return

explanation: Well done! Always start with Standard Precautions for every new admission until specific lab results or doctor's orders guide you otherwise. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T4#GNS313_U2_T4_h2)

question: Why does adaptive immunity fight off a familiar germ much faster and stronger the second time around?

options.A: Because innate barriers disappear over time
options.B: Because the germ becomes weaker inside the body
options.C: Because it creates immunological memory
options.D: Because white blood cells multiply without stopping

explanation: Spot on! Your adaptive immune system keeps memory cells from past infections so it can launch a fast, targeted attack if the germ returns. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T83#GNS214_U1_T83_h2)

question: Why is secondary prevention so crucial for conditions like type 2 diabetes?

options.A: The disease often develops silently without early symptoms
options.B: Symptoms are always too painful to ignore
options.C: Early detection makes the condition completely disappear
options.D: Screening tests are expensive and rarely performed

explanation: Exactly! Type 2 diabetes can creep up quietly for years without symptoms, making routine screening an absolute lifesaver. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T17#GNS222_U2_T17_h3)

question: What should a nurse manager do if evaluation reveals that a newly implemented patient safety plan failed to reduce medication errors?

options.A: Stop collecting data on medication errors entirely
options.B: Immediately fire all nurses working on the affected unit
options.C: Analyze what went wrong, adjust the strategy, and try again
options.D: Pretend the results do not exist and file the report away

explanation: Management planning is a continuous cycle; when a plan falls short, the manager must revise it and adapt. [learn more](GST321_U1_T5#GST321_U1_T5_h7)

question: A healthy term baby develops mild yellow skin on day three of life, which gradually disappears by day ten without treatment. How is this classified?

options.A: Kernicterus syndrome
options.B: Pathological hemolysis
options.C: Physiological jaundice
options.D: Bile duct obstruction

explanation: Jaundice that appears after 24 hours, peaks early, and resolves on its own within two weeks in a healthy infant is normal physiological jaundice. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h3)

question: What is the difference between client privacy and client confidentiality?

options.A: Privacy refers to hospital finances, whereas confidentiality refers to drug stock inventories
options.B: Privacy is a legal rule, whereas confidentiality is merely a personal suggestion
options.C: Privacy applies only to doctors, while confidentiality applies exclusively to nursing assistants
options.D: Privacy involves the client's body and physical space, whereas confidentiality involves keeping health information secret

explanation: Privacy protects physical boundaries, while confidentiality protects verbal and written medical data shared in professional trust. [learn more](GST321_U10_T5#GST321_U10_T5_h5)

question: What is the main advantage of Artemisinin-based Combination Therapy (ACT)?

options.A: Making the medication taste significantly sweeter for children
options.B: Eliminating the need for any laboratory blood tests
options.C: Preventing drug resistance and clearing remaining parasites
options.D: Allowing the entire treatment course to last only one hour

explanation: Spot on! Combining a fast-acting drug with a partner drug clears the malaria completely and stops resistant strains from developing. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T5#GNS223_U3_T5_h4)

question: What is the main goal when giving culturally sensitive nutrition counseling?

options.A: To eliminate all traditional cooking methods from the community
options.B: To adapt healthy eating advice to fit the patient's local lifestyle and foods
options.C: To replace all local food items with expensive imported supplements
options.D: To force every patient to adopt a westernized diet style

explanation: Good nursing care works with what the patient already eats and enjoys, making healthy lifestyle changes realistic and sustainable. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T017#GNS227_U2_T017_h7)

question: Which protein in the blood is the main carrier for drugs?

options.A: Albumin
options.B: Globulin
options.C: Fibrinogen
options.D: Hemoglobin

explanation: Albumin is the most common protein in our blood plasma. It acts like a taxi service, carrying many different drugs around the body. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T2#GNS125_U5_T2_h3)

question: A patient is staring blankly, speaking very little, and showing no emotion after an accident. What are they likely experiencing?

options.A: Aggressive hostility
options.B: Emotional numbness
options.C: Delusional psychosis
options.D: Hyper-arousal panic

explanation: Spot on! Right after trauma, a patient's mind can freeze up or go numb, making them look quiet, blank, and detached. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T9#GNS112_U7_T9_h2)

question: Which Nigerian food item is an excellent local source of both plant protein and healthy fats?

options.A: Melon seeds (egusi)
options.B: Refined white sugar
options.C: Packaged soft drinks
options.D: Polished white garri

explanation: Spot on! Egusi is packed with valuable plant proteins and healthy fats, making it a powerhouse for local nutrition. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T004#GNS227_U3_T004_h6)

question: A patient is terrified to tell their spouse about their HIV diagnosis. What is a helpful nursing action?

options.A: Contact the spouse immediately without telling the patient
options.B: Tell the patient that spouses never react with anger
options.C: Offer to help prepare for the conversation through role-play
options.D: Advise the patient to keep the diagnosis a secret forever

explanation: You got this! Role-playing and talking through the steps helps build the patient's confidence to share their status safely. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T6#GNS216_U6_T6_h6)

question: What are the three components of the epidemiological triangle?

options.A: Vector, vaccine, and immunity
options.B: Agent, host, and environment
options.C: Bacteria, virus, and fungus
options.D: Primary, secondary, and tertiary

explanation: The classic epidemiological model uses the agent, host, and environment to explain how diseases are transmitted. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T4#GNS225_U2_T4_h5)

question: How does chronic viral hepatitis usually behave differently from acute hepatitis in the early stages?

options.A: Chronic infections often cause no symptoms for many years while silently damaging the liver
options.B: Chronic infections always start with a sudden, violent fever and severe vomiting
options.C: Chronic infections resolve completely within two to four weeks without any treatment
options.D: Chronic infections only affect older adults with pre-existing kidney disease

explanation: That's why chronic strains like Hepatitis B and C can be so tricky—they can hide out in the body for years without giving any warning signs! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T16#GNS313_U2_T16_h4)

question: How do emergency contraceptive pills work after unprotected sex?

options.A: By thickening the uterine wall to trap the fertilized egg inside
options.B: By delaying or preventing the release of an egg from the ovary
options.C: By permanently destroying all active sperm inside the fallopian tubes
options.D: By causing an immediate surgical termination of an implanted embryo

explanation: Emergency contraceptives act like a pause button on ovulation. They push back the release of the egg so the sperm simply die out waiting. Simple and effective! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T17#GNS215_U6_T17_h4)

question: A nurse asks her current study participants to help her connect with other patients who have the same rare condition. What method is this?

options.A: Systematic sampling
options.B: Snowball sampling
options.C: Cluster sampling
options.D: Stratified sampling

explanation: Brilliant! Just like a snowball rolling down a hill and getting bigger, snowball sampling grows as participants introduce you to their friends. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T14#GNS217_U3_T14_h4)

question: What is the primary vector responsible for transmitting Lassa fever in endemic regions?

options.A: Multimammate rats
options.B: Domesticated pigs
options.C: Tsetse flies
options.D: Anopheles mosquitoes

explanation: Lassa fever is primarily transmitted to humans through contact with food or items contaminated by infected multimammate rodents. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T1#GNS313_U2_T1_h5)

question: What does antimicrobial resistance mean?

options.A: The human immune system destroys all beneficial bacteria
options.B: Microbes change and survive treatment with standard medications
options.C: Antibiotics lose their expiration date while on the shelf
options.D: Patients develop an allergic reaction to powerful drugs

explanation: Resistance happens when germs mutate or adapt so that drugs that used to kill them no longer work. [learn more](GST114_U1_T3#GST114_U1_T3_h4)

question: Why are Class IV drugs effective for treating supraventricular tachycardia?

options.A: They completely eliminate all electrical activity in the heart wall
options.B: They speed up the natural pacemaker cells in the right atrium
options.C: They slow down conduction through the atrioventricular node
options.D: They force the ventricles to beat faster than the upper chambers

explanation: By slowing AV node conduction, these drugs break the rapid loop causing supraventricular tachycardia. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T3#GNS223_U1_T3_h6)

question: Why is an elevated pulse often considered an early warning sign of patient distress?

options.A: The heart speeds up to compensate before blood pressure drops
options.B: Fever always causes immediate kidney failure if left untreated
options.C: It proves the patient is simply feeling nervous about hospital food
options.D: A fast pulse means the lungs have stopped absorbing oxygen entirely

explanation: The body increases the heart rate to maintain adequate blood flow and pressure when stress, blood loss, or illness occurs. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T8#GNS111_U2_T8_h6)

question: You wear sterile gloves and a mask while putting in a urinary catheter. Which link in the infection chain are you mainly trying to block?

options.A: Reservoir
options.B: Portal of entry
options.C: Susceptible host
options.D: Infectious agent

explanation: Awesome! Using sterile barriers blocks germs from sneaking into vulnerable places like the urinary tract. [learn more](GST114_U2_T1#GST114_U2_T1_h7)

question: What tends to happen to the basal metabolic rate during long periods of severe calorie restriction?

options.A: It fluctuates every single hour
options.B: It slows down to conserve energy
options.C: It stops functioning completely
options.D: It increases to burn extra glucose

explanation: Correct! Your body is smart—when it senses very low food intake, it slows down its metabolism to save energy, which can make further weight loss slower. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T010#GNS227_U6_T010_h5)

question: Why might the standard 0-to-10 numeric pain scale be tricky to use for an adult with severe dementia?

options.A: Numeric scales only work for surgical wounds
options.B: Patients with dementia lose the ability to speak at all
options.C: They will always just say ten no matter what
options.D: They may struggle to connect a number to how they feel

explanation: Well reasoned! Numbers are abstract concepts. For patients with cognitive changes, we often need to rely on facial expression charts or physical behavior cues instead. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T7#GNS221_U3_T7_h4)

question: Why don't we use traditional validity and reliability tests in qualitative research?

options.A: Computers cannot calculate statistics on words the same way they do numbers
options.B: Qualitative researchers do not care if their findings are accurate or true
options.C: Human experiences are subjective and cannot be measured with rigid consistency
options.D: Ethics boards forbid researchers from testing qualitative data for errors

explanation: Human feelings and experiences change and cannot be put into a rigid numerical box, so qualitative research uses different checks for quality. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T6#GNS224_U1_T6_h7)

question: Which of the following is the first link in the chain of infection?

options.A: Mode of transmission
options.B: Infectious agent
options.C: Portal of entry
options.D: Susceptible host

explanation: The chain always starts with the actual germ or infectious agent itself before it finds a home. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T81#GNS214_U1_T81_h2)

question: How must controlled medications like morphine be kept safe on a hospital ward?

options.A: Unlocked inside the general treatment room
options.B: In an open plastic tray on the main desk
options.C: Inside the patient's bedside drawer for privacy
options.D: Inside a double-locked secure cupboard

explanation: Correct! Controlled drugs are powerful and prone to abuse, so they always live in a secure double-locked space. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T13#GNS125_U2_T13_h5)

question: What do we call the temporary germs you pick up while touching patients that cause most hospital infections?

options.A: Transient flora
options.B: Fungal spores
options.C: Endogenous flora
options.D: Resident flora

explanation: Transient flora are just passing through! You pick them up during patient care, and thankfully, regular hand washing easily washes them away. [learn more](GST114_U2_T6#GST114_U2_T6_h2)

question: A patient tells you they only want a general idea of their condition and do not want all the technical details. What is the most appropriate nursing response?

options.A: Tell their family members the full medical report instead
options.B: Insist they hear everything so they can make informed choices
options.C: Respect their preference and provide a clear, high-level summary
options.D: Refuse to talk to them until they agree to hear all test results

explanation: Patients have the right to guide how much information they receive, and nurses should honor these individual preferences. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T6#GNS321_U4_T6_h3)

question: Why do young children with sickle cell anaemia take daily preventive penicillin?

options.A: To thin the blood and stop red blood cells from clumping together
options.B: To stimulate the bone marrow to create more red blood cells
options.C: To lower the body temperature and prevent sudden high fevers
options.D: To protect against severe infections caused by functional asplenia

explanation: Over time, sickle cell damage makes the spleen stop working well (functional asplenia). Because the spleen is vital for fighting certain bacteria, daily penicillin acts as a shield to keep these kids safe from severe infections. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T7#GNS311_U2_T7_h7)

question: How do family planning 'supply methods' differ mainly from long-acting methods like coils or implants?

options.A: They can only be obtained through a surgical procedure
options.B: They provide permanent sterilization after a single use
options.C: They are inserted by a doctor and last for five years
options.D: They require active user action during or before every sexual act

explanation: Supply methods rely entirely on you remembering to use them correctly each time, unlike implants or coils that work continuously in the background. You've got this! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T5#GNS225_U3_T5_h1)

question: A client wants a refill for her birth control, but admits she might already be pregnant. What should you do first?

options.A: Perform a pregnancy test before giving the refill
options.B: Tell her to double her dose for the next week
options.C: Switch her to a progestin-only pill right away
options.D: Refill the prescription immediately without questions

explanation: Safety first! Always rule out an existing pregnancy before continuing hormonal contraceptives to protect both the client and potential pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T012#GNS226_U6_T012_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier faced by patients needing rehabilitation?

options.A: Physical barriers like stairs and narrow doors
options.B: Negative cultural beliefs and social stigma
options.C: Excessive availability of trained therapists in rural areas
options.D: High financial costs for care and equipment

explanation: Correct! Rural areas unfortunately suffer from a serious shortage of healthcare workers, not an oversupply of them. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T5#GNS225_U2_T5_h7)

question: What is the most important infection control practice for nurses doing perineal care or dressing changes?

options.A: Using scented antiseptic soaps for all skin surfaces
options.B: Wearing sterile gowns for routine temperature checks
options.C: Isolating the mother from her newborn baby
options.D: Rigorous hand hygiene and aseptic technique

explanation: Simple hand hygiene and clean sterile technique are your absolute best defenses against bringing new germs into healing wounds. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T024#GNS226_U3_T024_h7)

question: What does the term 'bereavement' mean in nursing care?

options.A: The physical pain felt in the chest after a loss
options.B: The deliberate suppression of sad emotions
options.C: The objective state of having lost someone through death
options.D: The outward religious rituals performed at a funeral

explanation: You've got this! Bereavement is simply the factual reality that someone you care about has passed away. It is the starting point where grief and mourning begin. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T10#GNS321_U4_T10_h1)

question: How would you best describe organizational culture in a hospital?

options.A: The official printed employee handbook issued at hiring
options.B: The shared values, beliefs, and unwritten rules of a workplace
options.C: The physical layout and architectural design of the building
options.D: The total annual financial revenue generated by the facility

explanation: Culture is the 'personality' of the ward—the unwritten habits, attitudes, and vibe shared by the healthcare team ("this is how we do things around here"). [learn more](GST321_U1_T1#GST321_U1_T1_h6)

question: What is the difference between substandard and counterfeit medications?

options.A: Substandard drugs are manufactured locally, while counterfeit drugs are always imported.
options.B: Counterfeit drugs are cheaper versions of safe generics produced by licensed companies.
options.C: Substandard drugs fail quality specifications, while counterfeit drugs are deliberately mislabeled copies.
options.D: Substandard drugs have expired dates, while counterfeit drugs contain too much active ingredient.

explanation: Substandard drugs are usually genuine products that missed quality marks, while counterfeits are fake, fraudulent copies made to deceive us. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T1#GNS215_U1_T1_h6)

question: What is a great trick to help a mum manage early morning pregnancy nausea?

options.A: Remaining completely fasting until the afternoon hours
options.B: Eating small, dry carbohydrate snacks before getting out of bed
options.C: Consuming a heavy, high-fat breakfast right away
options.D: Drinking a large cup of cold whole milk immediately upon waking

explanation: Such a classic nursing tip! A dry biscuit before standing up keeps blood sugar stable and calms that empty, nauseous tummy. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T008#GNS227_U2_T008_h6)

question: Which of these is a common limitation of economic appraisals in healthcare?

options.A: They guarantee that hospitals will never experience financial shortages
options.B: They require every nurse to become a certified health economist
options.C: They eliminate the need for clinical judgment in patient diagnoses
options.D: They rely on assumptions and data that may not match real-world emergencies

explanation: Economic models are great on paper, but real hospital wards are chaotic and unpredictable. Models can miss sudden clinical emergencies. [learn more](GST322_U2_T5#GST322_U2_T5_h7)

question: Why does food taste so bland when you have a bad cold and a stuffy nose?

options.A: Flavor perception depends heavily on olfaction working alongside taste buds
options.B: Mucus completely paralyzes the taste buds on the surface of the tongue
options.C: Cold viruses attack and destroy the nerves responsible for sensing sweet foods
options.D: Swelling in the throat blocks the physical swallowing of food particles

explanation: Your tongue only handles the basics (sweet, sour, salty, bitter, umami). Most of what you call 'flavor' is actually your sense of smell working overtime while you chew! [learn more](GNS311_U3_T1#GNS311_U3_T1_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of using a partograph during labor?

options.A: To monitor labor progress and spot any danger early
options.B: To record the birth weight of the baby
options.C: To measure the mother's daily food intake
options.D: To calculate the hospital bill

explanation: You got it! The partograph gives nurses a clear picture of how labor is going, helping you quickly catch prolonged labor or fetal distress. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T004#GNS226_U1_T004_h4)

question: Why is checking a patient's pulse such a useful assessment tool in daily nursing care?

options.A: It determines the total volume of fluid in the entire body
options.B: It gives direct clues about heart pumping efficiency and blood flow
options.C: It shows whether the lungs are exchanging gases properly
options.D: It measures the exact amount of oxygen inside the red blood cells

explanation: The pulse rate and rhythm reflect how effectively the heart is working as a pump and delivering blood to peripheral tissues. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T8#GNS111_U2_T8_h1)

question: What is considered the single most effective method to prevent the spread of infections in a clinical setting?

options.A: Routine room painting
options.B: Proper hand hygiene
options.C: Wearing rubber boots
options.D: Administering vitamins

explanation: Regular and thorough hand washing or sanitizing removes transient microorganisms acquired from touching patients and contaminated surfaces. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T95#GNS214_U1_T95_h4)

question: Which organ in the body is the main target for both Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C?

options.A: The lungs
options.B: The pancreas
options.C: The kidneys
options.D: The liver

explanation: Spot on! Both hepatitis B and C viruses attack liver cells, causing inflammation and long-term damage if left untreated. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h3)

question: Why do healthy pregnant women need to produce more insulin as their pregnancy advances?

options.A: The growing fetus directly destroys maternal pancreatic cells
options.B: The liver stores less glucose as pregnancy progresses
options.C: Placental hormones make maternal cells more resistant to insulin
options.D: Maternal kidneys begin to excrete insulin much faster

explanation: As the placenta grows, it releases hormones that create insulin resistance, forcing the pancreas to pump out extra insulin to keep blood sugar stable. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T006#GNS226_U4_T006_h1)

question: What should a nurse tell a patient taking liquid iron syrup to prevent staining their teeth?

options.A: Drink the liquid through a straw and rinse your mouth afterwards.
options.B: Take the medication right before lying down to go to sleep at night.
options.C: Brush your teeth vigorously immediately after swallowing the dose.
options.D: Mix the iron directly into a full glass of whole milk before drinking.

explanation: Liquid iron can easily stain teeth! Using a straw bypasses the teeth, and rinsing washes away any lingering drops. Simple practical nursing advice! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T9#GNS215_U6_T9_h8)

question: Why is Primary Health Care called the first point of contact in a health system?

options.A: It operates only inside large national teaching hospitals
options.B: It is where individuals and families first seek guidance and basic care
options.C: It exclusively handles complex surgical procedures and intensive care
options.D: It requires a referral letter from a specialist before a patient can visit

explanation: PHC is the open front door of healthcare where community members go first for everyday health needs and routine checkups. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h1)

question: At what point in the procedure should you release the tourniquet?

options.A: Immediately after the first blood tube is filled
options.B: Before pulling the needle out of the vein
options.C: Before inserting the needle into the skin
options.D: After applying the adhesive bandage to the arm

explanation: Remember to release the tourniquet before taking the needle out. This stops extra blood from leaking out and prevents a nasty bruise from forming. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h6)

question: A nurse notices an unsteady resident pacing near a cluttered hallway. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Administer a strong sedative medication to keep the resident asleep
options.B: Ignore the situation since walking independently is always encouraged
options.C: Clear the hallway clutter and assist the resident safely back to their seat
options.D: Instruct the resident to run down the hallway to improve agility

explanation: You've got it! Clearing out obstacles right away is a quick, life-saving step to prevent falls. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T2#GNS324_U5_T2_h6)

question: Why do HMOs place a strong emphasis on preventive health services?

options.A: To increase the out-of-pocket bills for the enrollees
options.B: To comply with international travel regulations
options.C: To force patients to visit doctors every single week
options.D: To catch illnesses early and lower expensive treatment costs

explanation: Preventing diseases or treating them early is much cheaper for the HMO than paying for complex, prolonged hospital admissions later. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h1)

question: Why is active listening an important skill in health promotion?

options.A: It helps the nurse uncover barriers stopping the patient from being healthy
options.B: It replaces the need to check vital signs or physical health
options.C: It shortens the time required for documentation paperwork
options.D: It guarantees the patient will never develop a chronic illness

explanation: Listening carefully lets nurses find out if fear, cost, or confusion is getting in the way of a patient's care. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T2#GNS225_U2_T2_h5)

question: Why is psychosocial support so important in internally displaced persons (IDP) camps?

options.A: To teach residents advanced corporate business management
options.B: To help residents cope with the mental trauma of displacement and loss
options.C: To replace the need for clean drinking water
options.D: To make sure people follow commercial tax rules

explanation: Spot on! Losing your home and community causes deep emotional pain. Mental health and psychosocial support are crucial for true healing and recovery. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T26#GNS225_U5_T26_h7)

question: What is another common name for a food-borne illness?

options.A: Bowel obstruction
options.B: Nutritional deficiency
options.C: Gastric influenza
options.D: Food poisoning

explanation: You've got this! 'Food poisoning' is simply the everyday term we use when someone gets sick from eating or drinking something contaminated. Keep going! [learn more](GNS227_U3_T010#GNS227_U3_T010_h1)

question: What can happen if you use the wrong liquid (diluent) to mix a vaccine?

options.A: It can destroy the vaccine or harm the client
options.B: It doubles the number of active doses inside the vial
options.C: It automatically turns the liquid into a bright blue color
options.D: It extends the expiration date by exactly six months

explanation: Every vaccine has a specific liquid made just for it. Using the wrong one ruins the dose and compromises patient safety. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T73#GNS214_U1_T73_h4)

question: A nurse reviews a high-quality study on a new pain management protocol. What local factor must be checked before introducing it to the ward?

options.A: Whether the ward has the staff training and resources to support the protocol
options.B: How many awards the primary investigator has won
options.C: Whether the original authors will visit the hospital to supervise
options.D: If the journal article has a colorful cover page

explanation: Research implementation must always consider local feasibility, including equipment, staff readiness, and institutional support. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T4#GNS224_U4_T4_h6)

question: Where is the subdural space normally found?

options.A: Between the skull bone and the outer dura mater

question: A patient just lost her home in a fire. She won't eat, stares at the wall, and speaks in whispers. What should the nurse do first?

question: What does the acronym SBAR stand for in nursing communication?

question: Which of these best describes emotional abuse?

question: What is the main goal when doing rehabilitation care for older adults?

question: What is a frequent cause of severe injuries on industrial cargo or work boats?

question: What does high bioavailability mean for a medication?

question: Which hormone does the body pump out in large amounts during long periods of stress?

question: What is the primary function of an enteric coating on a tablet?

question: A patient in a rural community stops coming for clinic refills because transport fare is more expensive than the drugs. What barrier is this?

question: Which of these is the best example of a clear, actionable goal for a nursing unit?

question: Why is it so tricky to spot an asymptomatic carrier during a disease outbreak?

question: A primary school pupil comes in with round, scaly, itchy patches on their head and some hair loss in those spots. What's the most likely issue?

question: Why does the Essential Drug Programme focus heavily on generic medicines instead of brand names?

question: What does the detrusor muscle do while your body is storing urine normally?

question: Why do you need to be extra careful with cleaning liquids on a smart bed?

question: Why would community health workers use megaphones in a local market before an immunization drive?

question: A nurse wants to address high salt intake in a local market. What should be the very first step?

question: Which of these is a classic life-saving action done during the primary survey?

question: How do vitamins mostly help our bodies work?

question: Which two common bacteria are most often responsible for causing salpingitis?

question: How does Rifampicin stop TB bacteria from multiplying?

question: What does 'active participation' mean when conducting a community health session?

question: Which psychological condition is commonly reported among survivors of FGM?

question: What is the main goal of performing a comprehensive nutritional assessment in a hospital setting?

question: What type of motivation drives a nurse who feels a deep personal pride and joy in helping patients recover?

options.A: Financial motivation

options.C: Intrinsic motivation

explanation: Think of intrinsic motivation as the fire that comes from within! It is driven by your personal sense of purpose, passion, and the genuine joy you feel when caring for your patients. [learn more](GST321_U3_T6#GST321_U3_T6_h1)

question: When is the best time to perform airway suctioning on a ventilated patient?

options.A: When clinical indicators like secretions or coughing are present

question: What is a very common complaint you will hear from patients who have anaemia?

question: Why does a cold swimming pool stop feeling so freezing after you stay in it for a few minutes?

question: What is the primary purpose of placing a drainage tube in a surgical wound?

question: As a nurse, what is your very first priority when a patient arrives with post-abortion complications?

question: When is a 'competing' (directive) conflict style actually the right move in a hospital?

question: A mum in long labour has dry lips, dark urine, and a fast pulse. What is your best immediate nursing action?

question: A patient has trouble swallowing (dysphagia) after a stroke. What kind of fluids are they likely given?

question: Roughly what percentage of a healthy adult human body is made up of water?

question: What usually happens when a patient is discharged with a poor transition plan?

question: Why is it important to teach patients how to navigate parties, weddings, and restaurants during dietary counselling?

question: When should a nurse consider referring a psychiatric client to a sheltered workshop?

question: What is the main goal of antenatal care for a pregnant mother?

question: Why is dietary counselling considered a collaborative process rather than just giving a printed diet sheet?

question: Why is a team approach (doctors, nurses, social workers) needed to help delinquent youths?

question: What does 'unity of command' mean during a disaster response?

question: What is the main purpose of an assisted living facility?

question: How should you best communicate with an older adult who has mild hearing loss?

question: What is the best approach for managing pain in an infant who has just been circumcised?

options.A: Applying ice packs directly to the bare surgical wound for hours
options.B: Administering strong opioid medications every two hours around the clock
options.C: Keeping the infant awake so they do not feel the post-surgical pain
options.D: Using sweet oral sucrose solution alongside prescribed mild pain relievers

explanation: Sweet sucrose drops combined with safe, mild pain meds (like paracetamol) provide great comfort and pain relief for babies. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T5#GNS311_U4_T5_h7)

question: Why do healthcare teams hold a debriefing session after a major disaster or emergency response?

options.A: To assign blame to specific individuals who made mistakes
options.B: To fulfill mandatory paperwork requirements with no practical use
options.C: To evaluate response performance and identify areas for system improvement
options.D: To decide which staff members should be terminated

explanation: Well done! Debriefs are meant to be a safe, constructive way to look at what went right and what we can do better next time. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T4#GNS315_U1_T4_h8)

question: What is a vital legal and clinical truth Nigerian nurses must know about post-abortion care?

options.A: Treating complications from an abortion is a legal, life-saving medical service
options.B: Nurses are legally required to report every PAC client to the police
options.C: Only medical doctors are legally permitted to provide post-abortion counseling
options.D: Emergency post-abortion treatment is prohibited by the national health act

explanation: Even with strict abortion laws, giving emergency medical care to save a woman from an incomplete or septic abortion is completely legal and necessary. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T025#GNS226_U5_T025_h6)

question: What is the main physiological purpose of the large intestine?

options.A: Producing bile salts to help break down dietary fats
options.B: Absorbing remaining water and compacting indigestible waste
options.C: Digesting complex proteins into single amino acids
options.D: Secreting hydrochloric acid to kill swallowed bacteria

explanation: By the time food residue gets to the colon, most nutrients are already gone. The large intestine's main task is to suck back the water and turn waste into solid stool. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T011#GNS227_U1_T011_h7)

question: What is the key trait of a polyvalent nurse?

options.A: Focusing exclusively on surgical nursing care
options.B: Training across multiple clinical specialties
options.C: Specializing in pediatric medicine only
options.D: Working only in hospital management roles

explanation: Spot on! A polyvalent nurse is cross-trained in different fields, meaning they can comfortably move and work across various hospital departments. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h1)

question: What is the very first thing you should do after an accidental needle-stick injury?

options.A: Cover the bleeding wound tightly with a waterproof bandage
options.B: Squeeze the puncture site firmly to force out old blood
options.C: Wash the affected area thoroughly with soap and water
options.D: Apply a strong antiseptic alcohol solution to seal the cut

explanation: Spot on! Don't panic. Calmly wash the area right away with plenty of soap and running water to flush out as many germs as possible. [learn more](GST114_U2_T21#GST114_U2_T21_h7)

question: What is the clinical benefit of providing a wide variety of choices in family planning services?

options.A: The clinic can avoid stocking pills and focus only on injectables
options.B: It eliminates all possible side effects associated with hormones
options.C: Clients can choose contraception that fits their personal lifestyle and health needs
options.D: Nurses can force every client to use long-acting contraceptives

explanation: Brilliant! Giving clients options respects their autonomy and helps them find a method that genuinely matches their lifestyle and health profile. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T4#GNS312_U5_T4_h6)

question: A postpartum patient is bleeding heavily and showing signs of shock. What is the most urgent vascular access step?

options.A: Insert two large-bore intravenous cannulas for rapid fluid replacement
options.B: Administer oral rehydration salts slowly through a nasogastric tube
options.C: Set up a single fine-needle peripheral line for routine daily hydration
options.D: Collect a midstream urine sample to check for urinary tract infection

explanation: In an emergency, large-bore IV lines let you pump in fluids and blood fast enough to rescue her blood pressure and beat shock. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h5)

question: A pregnant patient with hyperemesis has low potassium and high blood pH. What is happening?

options.A: Respiratory acidosis
options.B: Metabolic acidosis
options.C: Respiratory alkalosis
options.D: Metabolic alkalosis

explanation: Pumping out stomach acid through continuous vomiting strips the body of hydrogen ions, causing blood pH to rise. That's metabolic alkalosis in action—keep smashing those lab values! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T016#GNS226_U2_T016_h3)

question: In diastolic heart failure, what is the main problem with how the heart works?

options.A: The electrical system fires at a very irregular rhythm
options.B: The heart muscle cannot relax and fill with blood properly
options.C: The heart muscle cannot squeeze hard enough to push blood out
options.D: The heart valves fail to open during pumping

explanation: In diastolic failure, the heart muscle gets stiff. It can squeeze okay, but it struggles to relax and fill up with enough blood first. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T12#GNS213_U1_T12_h3)

question: A clinical trial claims a new bandage prevents infections, but later studies show it doesn't. What type of error happened?

options.A: Descriptive error
options.B: Type II error
options.C: Sampling error
options.D: Type I error

explanation: You nailed it! Believing an intervention works when it's actually useless is a classic false positive, which is a Type I error. Keep crushing it! [learn more](GNS217_U4_T3#GNS217_U4_T3_h5)
